images.caption: 316 Bowery on the corner of Bleecker Street in Manhattan, New York City, was built in 1868 for banker Robert Irwin and was known as the Irwin Building, designed by Nicholas Whyte.  It is in use as a condominium apartment building. {Source: Daytonian in Manhattan)

images.caption: The Hardenbrook-Somarindyck House, a Federal-style house at 135 Bowery between Grand and Broome Streets in the Lower East Side neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City was built c.1817.  It was designated a New York City landmark on June 28, 2011, but that designation was overturned by the City Council in September 2011. (Sources: "NYCLPC Hardenbrook-Somarindyck House Designation Report", News report)
images.alt: The Hardenbrook-Somarindyck House, a Federal-style house at 135 Bowery between Grand and Broome Streets in the Lower East Side neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City was built c.1817.  It was designated a New York City landmark on June 28, 2011, but that designation was overturned by the City Council in September 2011. (Sources: "NYCLPC Hardenbrook-Somarindyck House Designation Report", News report)
